lines.text: Right now, invisible waves are flying through your body, carrying videos, messages, and memes. That's Wi-Fi.
Wi-Fi is just radio. The same kind of wave as your car radio, but much faster. About two to six billion wiggles every second.
To send data, the router changes the wave. A little taller, a little shifted. Each tiny change means some ones and zeros.
Modern Wi-Fi packs about a thousand different wave shapes, so every single wiggle can carry ten bits at once.
And it doesn't use just one wave. It splits the channel into hundreds of thin lanes, all sending side by side.
Walls, water and even your body soak up some of the signal. That's why the far bedroom gets one bar.
Everyone in the room shares the same air. So devices take turns, thousands of times a second, so fast it feels like nobody waits.
And because everyone on the same Wi-Fi shares one network, Orbi Transfer can show you what's being shared nearby. No login, no contacts, no Bluetooth pairing.
